record.paper_title: Topological Open Problems in the Geometry of Banach Spaces
record.context_brief: LUR renorming of C(K) for separable Rosenthal compacta
record.original_question: Let K be a separable Rosenthal compact space, meaning a compact space of Baire-one functions on a Polish space. Must the Banach space C(K) of continuous scalar-valued functions on K admit an equivalent locally uniformly rotund renorming?

evidence.quote: The former result fits in the study of compact spaces K ⊂ RΓ formed with Baire one functions on a Polish space Γ, the so called Rosenthal compacta.
Question 8. If K is a separable Rosenthal compact then does it follow that C(K) admits an equivalent locally uniformly rotund renorming?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Polish space is a separable, completely metrizable topological space. Given a Polish space $\Gamma$, let $B_1(\Gamma)$ denote the set of Baire-class-one real functions on $\Gamma$ (pointwise limits of sequences of continuous functions), endowed with the topology of pointwise convergence. A compact Hausdorff space $K$ is called a Rosenthal compact if it is homeomorphic to a pointwise-compact subset of $B_1(\Gamma)$ for some Polish space $\Gamma$. Such a $K$ is called separable if it contains a countable dense subset.

For a compact Hausdorff space $K$, let $C(K)$ denote the Banach space of continuous scalar-valued functions on $K$ with the supremum norm. A norm $\|\cdot\|$ on a Banach space $X$ is locally uniformly rotund (LUR) if for every $x \in X$ and every sequence $(x_n)$ in $X$ with $\|x_n\| \to \|x\|$ and $\|x_n + x\| \to 2\|x\|$, one has $\|x_n - x\| \to 0$. A Banach space admits an equivalent LUR renorming if there exists an LUR norm equivalent to its original norm.

Question: Must $C(K)$ admit an equivalent locally uniformly rotund renorming whenever $K$ is a separable Rosenthal compact?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to remain open in general. Partial positive results are known: when each function in the Rosenthal compact $K \subset B_1(\Gamma)$ has only countably many points of discontinuity, $C(K)$ admits an equivalent pointwise lower semicontinuous LUR norm (Moltó–Orihuela–Troyanski and related work). The full conjecture for arbitrary separable Rosenthal compacta is still cited as an open problem in subsequent surveys and papers on renorming theory.

status_evidence.title: Spaces of functions with countably many discontinuities
status_evidence.snippet: For a separable Rosenthal compact K representable as a space of functions with only countably many discontinuities in a Polish space, C(K) admits an LUR norm equivalent to the supremum norm.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: LUR renorming established for the subclass of separable Rosenthal compacta consisting of functions with countably many discontinuities.

status_evidence.title: On Compacta K for Which C(K) Has Some Good Renorming Properties
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture: If K is a separable Rosenthal compact then C(K) admits a locally uniformly rotund norm.
status_evidence.claim: The general statement is still presented as a conjecture/open problem in survey-style work.
